subject: Dedicated onboard: procurement gating, OEM quote lock, and cloud backstop
messages:
From: Alex Lee <alex@auroraai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitalcloud.com, sales_ops@vega-solutions.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity request and initial timelines for dedicated deployment

Sofia — thanks again for the call this morning. Aurora is planning a dedicated cluster for our customer-facing inference tier. High-level asks: ~200 A100-equivalent GPUs (estimated steady-state Q1 2027), expected go-live window: mid-March 2027.

Two immediate questions for Redwood to confirm so we can align procurement timelines: 
- What are the OEM lead times you are seeing today if we request a quote and commit? Any expedited options?
- Can Redwood provide a cloud-reserve backstop (short-term reserved slots in Orbital/partner clouds) to bridge OEM delivery gaps?

I've attached our current SOW draft for reference (Aurora_Dedicated_SOW_v3.pdf) and copied our procurement team at Orbital (procurement@orbitalcloud.com). We can be flexible on exact GPU SKU as long as you provide a deterministic plan for performance and cost.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync this week if helpful.

—Alex
Product Lead, Aurora AI
attachments: Aurora_Dedicated_SOW_v3.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Lee <alex@auroraai.com>, procurement@orbitalcloud.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity request and initial timelines for dedicated deployment

Thanks Alex — sharing internally to align procurement gating and short-term capacity options. Quick read for the group below, and proposed gating cadence so we can translate Aurora's March target into procurement milestones.

Priority items we need to lock: 
1) OEM quote lock date — vendor pricing windows have tightened; we should set a cut-off to accept OEM pricing (recommendation: 2026-12-05). After that any reorder will likely carry a longer lead time and different SKU mix.
2) Deposit and SOW sign-off — to trigger OEM manufacturing lane and reserve serials. Legal + Finance need a signed SOW + 30% deposit before we escalate to vendor.
3) Cloud backstop commitment — request Orbital (cc'd) to hold short-term reserved capacity for Aurora from Jan–Mar 2027 at defined rates, so we can meet the product go-live if OEM slips.
4) Sizing confirmation — Ben, can you produce a SKU mapping (A100 equiv -> preferred vendor SKUs + quantization profiles) and a revised cost delta for expedited delivery vs. normal fulfillment?

Next steps I propose: 
- Ben to confirm vendor ETA and send OEM quote spreadsheet (deadline: EOD 2026-11-25).
- Karthik to review whether dedicated onramp requires staggered tranche (Q1 vs Q2) and how that changes autoscaling config.
- Marissa to own the DocuSign SOW flow and confirm internal approval SLA.

If anyone thinks the quote-lock date should be earlier/later, flag now. Otherwise I'll send this as a formal gating checklist to Aurora with the DocuSign link once Ben shares the OEM numbers.

—Sofia
Program Manager, Dedicated Capacity

Folks — I spoke to Orbital procurement and Vega (our hardware integrator). Key points from vendor calls and a short action summary below. OEM quote attached (OEM_quote_Orbital_20261122.xlsx).

Vendor signals: 
- Baseline lead time for the preferred A100-equivalent SKU is ~18–20 weeks from PO. That aligns with current market lanes.
- Expedited lane: vendors can prioritize a 12-week slot for a ~12–15% premium and requires confirmed PO + 40% deposit within 5 business days of quote lock.
- Inventory carve-outs: we can request a short initial tranche (50 GPUs) that vendors can pull from stock within 6 weeks to enable a phased onramp.

Proposed timelines (assuming quote-lock 2026-12-05): 
- 2026-12-06 to 2026-12-12: finalize PO and deposit (if we take expedited lane).
- 2027-01-15 to 2027-02-15: phased arrivals of stock tranche (first 50 delivered under inventory carve-out).
- 2027-03-10 to 2027-04-30: bulk fulfillment (12–20 week standard lane).

Cloud backstop options: 
- Orbital can commit reserved instances for Jan–Mar at negotiated daily burn, but it is a time-limited reservation and we'd need contract language that releases us when OEM inventory arrives.
- Cost tradeoff: short-term cloud backstop at list rates will increase Opex vs. planned Capex; we should show Aurora the TCO delta.

Attachments: OEM_quote_Orbital_20261122.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Action items: 
- Karthik: confirm if we want staged tranches or all-in delivery assumption for capacity planning.
- Marissa: prepare DocuSign SOW and internal approval routing.
- Sofia: if you approve quote-lock = 2026-12-05, I will send the formal PO template to Aurora and request deposit terms.

Ben
Senior Supply Lead, Redwood Inference

2) Deposit: 40% required for expedited lane, payable within 5 business days of PO submission.
3) Phased onramp: first tranche = 50 GPUs (inventory carve-out) — arrival window 6–8 weeks after PO.
4) Cloud backstop: Orbital to hold reserved capacity Jan–Mar 2027 with automatic release on OEM delivery (contract clause to be added).
5) DocuSign SOW: link + expected sign-by date: 2026-12-08.
